subject: Application - Data Platform Engineer (m/f/d), Berlin
paragraphs: I am applying for the Data Platform Engineer role in Berlin. A platform whose users are the analysts, scientists and engineers above it, where the work is to make reliable data available and then get out of the way, is the job I have been doing for the last four years with a much smaller payload: thirteen hosts that exist so other people's work can run, and a task interface that is the only way anything gets changed. What I want next is the same role with real event volume under it and colleagues to argue with about it.

The infrastructure side is where I would start contributing. My platform is one flake that declares every host, with an SSH certificate authority, SOPS-encrypted secrets per host, and a task control plane as the operator surface, so a change is reviewed and gated before it exists rather than clicked into being; that habit transfers to Terraform and GitLab pipelines even though the tool does not. Reliability is recorded rather than assumed: a sentinel writes job status, generation age, disk and pressure-stall figures to a ledger every fifteen minutes and pages when a state is not ok, and the services on top are Go, Python and Bash with a PostgreSQL-backed mail archive among them. Python is my working language for the glue and the tooling, and on-call is not a rotation I am joining for the first time: it is my own pager, and alert noise is a defect I remove.

The gaps are specific, so I will name them. I have not run Kafka, Snowflake or Datadog: my fleet has no event stream, no warehouse and no hosted observability, and the closest equivalents are systemd journals, a ledger table and gatus checks, which is a different craft at a different scale. Terraform, GitLab CI and PySpark are not in my hands either; my infrastructure-as-code is Nix, which reconciles a whole machine from declared state, so the model is familiar but your tools would be new. Kubernetes is the same story: my hosts are single-tenant and separated by role, and the isolation I have built is a certificate authority and a module boundary rather than namespaces and quotas. And my event volume is a sentinel writing every fifteen minutes, not millions of events a day, so I would be learning what breaks first at that scale rather than recognising it.

One thing about Berlin deserves a straight answer rather than a line about being flexible. I live in Gutach im Breisgau, in south-west Germany near Freiburg, which is roughly seven hours from Berlin by train; an office-first hybrid team needs someone in the office, and I am not going to pretend a weekly commute is that. I hold German permanent residence and work here without restriction, so moving to Berlin is a domestic relocation with no permit attached, and if the role is office-first I would do it rather than ask for an exception. I would welcome a conversation about which part of the platform you would hand me first, and what I would need to learn fastest.
